title: Correctness of the Oblivious Simulator
statement: Let $W$ and $M$ be finite Turing machines over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be a binary language, and let $a,b$ be natural numbers and $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for every binary word $x$, $W$ outputs the binary expansion of $T(|x|)$ within $b(T(|x|)+1)$ steps; that $n\le T(n)$ for every $n$; and that $M$ decides $L$ within $aT(n)$ steps. Then for every binary word $x$, the simulator constructed from $W$, $M$, and $a$ on the input obtained by embedding each bit of $x$ into the schedule alphabet halts at some time $t$ with output consisting of the single schedule symbol whose bit tag is the indicator of whether $x\in L$.
hypotheses_covered: $W$ outputs $(T(|x|))$ in binary within $b(T(|x|)+1)$ steps for every binary word $x$
replaced:
Let $W$ compute on every input $x$ the binary expansion of $T(|x|)$ within
$b\,(T(|x|)+1)$ steps, suppose $n \le T(n)$ for all $n$, and let $M$ decide the
language $L$ within time $a\,T(n)$.  Then for every word $x$ there is a time $t$
within which the logical simulator, on the embedded input, computes the
one-symbol output consisting of the bit symbol of the indicator of $L$ at $x$.
